THE WELL LISTED KIT: ALL PROMPTS (version 1.0)

[A01] All-in-one Vinted listing
Use it when: You want a Vinted title, description and field values in one go.
----------------------------------------
Write a Vinted listing in UK English using ONLY these facts.

What it is: [E.G. JUMPER]
Brand: [BRAND OR "UNBRANDED"]
Size on label: [SIZE]
Measurements, laid flat (cm): [E.G. PIT TO PIT 51, LENGTH 63]
Colour: [COLOUR]
Material (from the label): [MATERIAL OR "NOT SURE"]
Condition: [NEW WITH TAGS / NEW WITHOUT TAGS / VERY GOOD / GOOD / SATISFACTORY]
Flaws (where, what, how big): [FLAWS OR "NONE FOUND"]
Anything else true: [E.G. "SMOKE-FREE HOME" OR "NONE"]

Give me:
1. A title of 60 characters or fewer: brand, item, colour, size. No padding.
2. A description of 50 to 120 words: what it is, size and measurements, condition with every flaw, material. End with one line inviting questions.
3. Values for Vinted's fields: category, brand, size, condition, colour, material.

Rules:
- If a fact is missing, write [CHECK: what is missing]. Never guess.
- Keep every flaw exactly as serious as I wrote it.
- No hype words, emoji or exclamation marks.
- Do not say rare, vintage, genuine or new unless I did. No other brand names.
- No payment, returns or contact details.

[A02] All-in-one eBay UK listing
Use it when: You want an eBay UK title, item specifics and description in one go.
----------------------------------------
Write an eBay UK listing in UK English using ONLY these facts.

What it is: [ITEM]
Brand: [BRAND OR "UNBRANDED"]
Model, style or product number: [OR "NOT SURE"]
Size on label: [SIZE OR "NOT APPLICABLE"]
Measurements or dimensions (cm): [MEASUREMENTS]
Colour: [COLOUR]
Material: [MATERIAL OR "NOT SURE"]
Condition: [E.G. NEW WITH TAGS / PRE-OWNED: GOOD]
Flaws (where, what, how big): [FLAWS OR "NONE FOUND"]
Tested (electricals only): [WHAT YOU TESTED, OR "NOT TESTED"]
Included / not included: [LIST]
Postage: [SERVICE]

Give me:
1. Two titles, 80 characters or fewer including spaces, with the count. Brand and item type first, then the details a buyer would search. Only true words, no padding.
2. Item specifics as a two-column table. Leave any I have not given as [CHECK].
3. A description under 200 words: what it is, measurements, condition with every flaw on its own line, what is included, postage.

Rules:
- Missing facts become [CHECK: what is missing]. Never guess.
- Keep every flaw. Do not soften any.
- No hype words, emoji or exclamation marks. No other brand names.
- Do not say rare, vintage, genuine, new or fully working unless I did.
- Nothing about returns or buyers' rights (I set those in eBay).

[A03] All-in-one Depop listing
Use it when: You want a Depop description (first line doing the job of a title) plus hashtags in one go.
----------------------------------------
Write a Depop listing in UK English using ONLY these facts.

What it is: [ITEM]
Brand: [BRAND OR "UNBRANDED"]
Size on label: [SIZE]
Measurements, laid flat (cm): [MEASUREMENTS]
Colour: [COLOUR]
Material: [MATERIAL OR "NOT SURE"]
Fit or style (only if true): [E.G. BOXY, CROPPED, 90S STYLE]
Era (only if you can back it up): [E.G. "1996 DATE ON LABEL" OR "UNKNOWN"]
Condition: [CONDITION]
Flaws (where, what, how big): [FLAWS OR "NONE FOUND"]

Give me one description under 800 characters, with the count:
1. First line: brand, item, colour, size and one honest style word. This acts as the title.
2. Two short lines on fit and details.
3. Measurements.
4. Condition with every flaw.
5. A last line of up to 5 relevant hashtags.

Rules:
- Missing facts become [CHECK: what is missing]. Never guess.
- Era words (90s, y2k, vintage) only if my era line supports them. Otherwise use "style" or leave them out.
- No hype, emoji strings or exclamation marks. No other brands in the text or hashtags.
- No payment or contact details.

[A04] All-in-one Etsy listing
Use it when: You make or sell handmade, vintage or craft supply items and want a title, tags and description in one go.
----------------------------------------
Write an Etsy listing in UK English using ONLY these facts.

What it is: [ITEM]
Handmade, vintage or craft supply: [TYPE]
Materials (all of them): [MATERIALS]
Size and weight: [DIMENSIONS]
Colours or options: [OPTIONS]
Personalisation (if any): [WHAT CAN CHANGE, CHARACTER LIMITS, OR "NONE"]
Made to order or ready to post, and dispatch time: [DETAILS]
Care instructions: [CARE]
Safety notes: [E.G. "NOT A TOY" OR "NONE"]
Condition and flaws (vintage only): [DETAILS OR "NOT APPLICABLE"]

Give me:
1. Two titles under 140 characters, with the count. A clear, readable phrase first, not a keyword list.
2. 13 tags, each 20 characters or fewer including spaces, with counts, then all 13 on one comma-separated line.
3. A description: two clear opening lines, then details, personalisation, dispatch, care and safety.

Rules:
- Missing facts become [CHECK: what is missing]. Never guess.
- Materials exactly as I wrote them. Do not upgrade "silver-plated" to "silver".
- No health or wellbeing claims (calming, healing, hypoallergenic). No hype words or exclamation marks.
- No other brands or characters. "Vintage" only if I gave an age of 20 years or more.

[A05] All-in-one Amazon UK listing
Use it when: You are a brand owner or seller of new stock creating an Amazon UK product listing.
----------------------------------------
Write an Amazon UK product listing in UK English using ONLY these facts.

Brand: [BRAND]
Product type: [PRODUCT]
Key features (only ones I can prove): [FEATURES]
Size, quantity or capacity: [DETAILS]
Colour: [COLOUR]
Materials: [MATERIALS]
What is in the box: [CONTENTS]
Care or use instructions: [DETAILS]
Is this a media product (books, music, video)? [YES / NO]

Give me:
1. A title of 75 characters or fewer including spaces (the rule for non-media categories from 27 July 2026), with the count.
2. An Item Highlights line of 125 characters or fewer, with the count, adding details not in the title.
3. Up to 5 bullet points, each a short label and one or two plain sentences.
4. A product description of 100 to 200 words.
5. Backend search terms: lower case, spaces only, no words already used above, under 240 bytes.

Rules:
- Missing facts become [CHECK: what is missing]. Never guess.
- Title: no ! $ ? _ { } ^ ¬ ¦ unless in the brand name, and no word more than twice (small words excepted).
- No promotional or subjective words (best, sale, free delivery, guaranteed), no emoji.
- No health, medical or eco claims. No other brand names anywhere.

[A06] All-in-one TikTok Shop UK listing
Use it when: You sell new stock or your own products on TikTok Shop UK and want a title, description and claims check in one go.
----------------------------------------
Write a TikTok Shop UK product listing in UK English using ONLY these facts.

Brand (mine, or one I am authorised to sell): [BRAND]
Product type: [PRODUCT]
Material: [MATERIAL]
Key features (only ones I can prove): [FEATURES]
Size, quantity or capacity: [DETAILS]
Colour or variant: [COLOUR]
What is included: [CONTENTS]
Care instructions: [CARE OR "NONE"]

Give me:
1. Three titles: brand, product type, material, key feature, then size, colour or quantity. At least 15 characters. Show the count.
2. A description of at least 30 words: one opening line, 4 short feature lines, "What's included", "Size and specs", "Care".
3. A list of any words I should double-check because they could count as a claim.

Rules:
- Missing facts become [CHECK: what is missing]. Never guess.
- Titles: no symbols, emoji, promotions (sale, x% off), shop name, web address, or mention of TikTok or other platforms.
- No claims that it cures, treats, prevents or relieves anything. No weight loss claims.
- No "best", no comparisons with other brands, no fake urgency, no vague green claims.

MODULE 01: THE LISTING BRIEF

[B01] Messy notes to Listing Brief
Use it when: You have jotted a few scrappy notes about an item and want a tidy brief.
----------------------------------------
Turn my notes below into a Listing Brief for a UK second-hand seller, using these headings:
Platform(s), What it is, Brand, Model or style, Size, Measurements (cm), Colour, Material, Condition, Flaws, Included, Not included, Age or era, Postage, Price.

Rules:
- UK English.
- Use ONLY facts in my notes. Do not add, assume or improve anything.
- If a heading has no information, write [CHECK: what I need to find out], e.g. [CHECK: measure pit to pit in cm].
- Keep every flaw exactly as serious as I wrote it.
- If I gave inches, show both (e.g. 21 in / 53 cm).
- No sales language. This is a fact sheet.
- At the end, list the 3 most important [CHECK] items a buyer would ask about.

My notes:
[PASTE YOUR NOTES HERE]

[B02] Voice note transcript to Listing Brief
Use it when: You talked about the item into your phone (quicker than typing) and have the transcript.
----------------------------------------
Below is a transcript of me talking about an item I am selling in the UK. It will ramble. Turn it into a Listing Brief with these headings:
What it is, Brand, Model or style, Size, Measurements (cm), Colour, Material, Condition, Flaws, Included, Not included, Tested (how), Postage, Price.

Rules:
- UK English.
- Where I corrected myself ("no wait, it's a 14"), use the correction only.
- Use ONLY facts I said. Do not fill gaps with typical details.
- Missing or unclear facts become [CHECK: ...].
- Transcription often mishears brands and numbers. If one looks odd, keep it and add [CHECK: transcript said "X", confirm spelling].
- Keep every flaw at the same level of seriousness. No sales language.

Transcript:
[PASTE TRANSCRIPT HERE]

[B03] Photo description to Listing Brief
Use it when: You want to describe what you can see, photo by photo, and turn it into a brief. The AI does not need to see images, so it works in any free tool.
----------------------------------------
I will describe my item photo by photo. Build a UK Listing Brief from my descriptions only, with these headings:
What it is, Brand, Model or style, Size, Measurements (cm), Colour, Material, Condition, Flaws (with location), Labels and markings (exact wording), Included, Postage, Price.

Rules:
- UK English. No sales language.
- Use only what I describe. Do not guess brand, age, material or value.
- For each flaw, record where and how big. If I gave no size, add [CHECK: size of flaw].
- After the brief, list extra photos a buyer would expect that I have not described (care label, base stamp, flaw close-up).

Photo 1: [DESCRIBE]
Photo 2: [DESCRIBE]
Photo 3: [DESCRIBE]
Price: [PRICE]
Postage: [POSTAGE]

[B04] Gap finder: what a buyer will ask
Use it when: You have a brief and want to catch the questions buyers will message you about.
----------------------------------------
Here is a Listing Brief for an item I am selling on [PLATFORM] in the UK. Act as a fussy buyer in this category.

1. List up to 8 questions a serious buyer would ask, most important first.
2. For each, say whether my brief answers it: Yes, No or Partly.
3. For every No or Partly, tell me what to check or measure and how, in plain words.

Do not write the listing. Do not invent answers. UK English, short lines.

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

[B05] Build my own category brief
Use it when: You sell a lot of one thing (bikes, prams, golf clubs, board games) and want a brief template made for it.
----------------------------------------
I sell second-hand [CATEGORY] in the UK on [PLATFORM(S)]. Create a reusable Listing Brief template for this category, as a plain text block I can copy into my notes app.

Include:
1. The general fields: platform, what it is, brand, model, size or dimensions, colour, material, condition, flaws, included, postage, price, lowest I will accept (private).
2. Up to 10 extra fields buyers of this category care about, each with a hint on where to find the fact, e.g. "frame size (printed on the seat tube)".
3. A short "safety and legal" list of things I should check before selling this category in the UK, written as questions for me to check in the platform's help pages. Do not state rules as fact.

UK English, plain words, no sales language.

[B06] Label or box text to Listing Brief
Use it when: You have a new or boxed item, or a clear product label, and want the facts copied off it accurately.
----------------------------------------
Below is text I copied from the box, label or manual of an item I am selling in the UK. Extract a Listing Brief with these headings:
What it is, Brand, Model / product number, Specification, Colour, Material, Dimensions, In the box, Safety or age warnings, Condition, Flaws, Postage, Price.

Rules:
- UK English.
- Copy specifications exactly. Do not round, convert or tidy numbers.
- Copy safety warnings and age guidance word for word.
- Leave marketing claims (e.g. "clinically proven") out of the brief. List them separately under "Box claims left out" so I can decide.
- Condition, flaws, postage and price are not on the box: write [CHECK: ...] unless I give them below.

Box or label text:
[PASTE TEXT HERE]

My extra details (condition, flaws, whether opened, postage, price):
[ADD DETAILS]

[B07] Brief tidy-up and consistency check
Use it when: Your brief is filled in and you want a sanity check before running the title and description prompts.
----------------------------------------
Check my Listing Brief for a UK [PLATFORM] listing. Do not rewrite it into a listing.

Report, in this order:
1. Contradictions (e.g. condition "Excellent" but flaws that sound like "Good").
2. Vague wording a buyer could dispute (e.g. "small mark" with no location or size), with a clearer version using only my facts.
3. Missing facts buyers in this category expect, as [CHECK: ...] lines.
4. Risky claims ("rare", "genuine", "fully working", "vintage" without an era, health claims), one line each on why.
5. US spellings or sizes to change.

UK English, short bullet points. Do not invent facts to fix problems. Ask me instead.

My Listing Brief:
[PASTE YOUR LISTING BRIEF HERE]

- Put the words a UK buyer would search first: brand, item type, then the most useful details (model, style, colour, material, size).
- 80 characters or fewer including spaces. Show the count after each.
- Use the space for true, searchable details from the brief. If you run out of true details, stop. Do not pad.

Rules:
- UK English and UK sizes ("UK 8" for shoes, "trousers" not "pants").
- Use ONLY facts in my brief. If a key search word is missing (e.g. model number), write [CHECK: model number] and tell me.
- No hype words, exclamation marks, emoji or whole words in capitals.
- No rare, vintage, genuine, new or limited edition unless the brief supports it. No other brand names. No repeated words.

[T07] Title tester: which version is clearest?
Use it when: You have 2 to 5 title ideas and want an honest, buyer's-eye comparison.
----------------------------------------
I am choosing a title for a [PLATFORM] UK listing. Here are my options and my Listing Brief.

For each title:
1. Count the characters including spaces. Say if it is over [LIMIT].
2. Give 3 short searches a UK buyer would likely type for this item, and say which ones each title matches.
3. Flag anything not in the brief, any hype, repeated words, or US spellings or sizes.
4. Say whether the first 40 characters (roughly what shows on a phone) make it clear what the item is.

Then recommend one in two lines. If you suggest a better version, use only facts from the brief. UK English.

Titles:
[PASTE TITLE 1]
[PASTE TITLE 2]
[PASTE TITLE 3]

My Listing Brief:

Write an eBay UK item description for the item in my Listing Brief below.

3. Condition: the grade, then every flaw on its own line with location, size and photo number if given.
4. Details: material, features, what is included and not included.
5. Postage: only what is in my brief.

Rules:
- UK English. Short lines. Under 200 words.
- Use ONLY facts in my brief. Missing facts become [CHECK: ...]. Never invent measurements, materials, dates or test results.
- Include every flaw. Do not soften or leave any out.
- No hype words, exclamation marks or emoji.
- No rare, vintage, genuine, fully working, new or smoke-free unless the brief says so.
- Do not reveal my lowest price. Nothing about returns (I set those in eBay).

[D06] Condition grader
Use it when: You are not sure which condition grade to choose, or which platform option matches.
----------------------------------------
Help me choose an honest condition grade for an item I am selling on [PLATFORM] in the UK.

Scale: New with tags, New without tags, Excellent, Very good, Good, Fair.
- If the item sits between two grades, choose the lower one.
- Base the grade only on what I list. Do not assume or ignore any flaw.

Then:
1. Give the grade and a one-line reason.
2. Name the closest option in [PLATFORM]'s condition list, and remind me to read the platform's own definition first.
3. Write a one or two line condition summary listing each flaw with location and size.
4. List anything I should check or photograph to be sure.

UK English. No softening words (barely, hardly, tiny) unless I used them, and never without a size.

Item: [WHAT IT IS]
Flaws and wear: [LIST EVERY FLAW]
Tags attached? [YES / NO]
Used or worn? [HOW OFTEN, IF KNOWN]

[D07] Flaw disclosure rewriter
Use it when: You wrote your flaws in a hurry and want them clear, specific and protective.
----------------------------------------
Rewrite the flaws below so they are clear and specific for a UK [PLATFORM] listing. A buyer should know exactly what to expect.

For each flaw, one line with: what it is, where it is (left and right as worn or used, and say so), how big (mm or cm), how visible (only if I said), and the photo number if I gave one.

Rules:
- UK English.
- Do not make any flaw sound smaller than I described it. Do not remove any.
- Missing size, location or visibility becomes [CHECK: ...].
- Add one line of what I checked and found fine, only from my list below.
- No reassurance words ("perfect otherwise"). Just facts.

My flaws, as I wrote them:
[PASTE FLAWS]

Things I checked and found fine:

UK English. Do not blame the buyer. Do not promise a delivery date. No cancelling or refunding outside the platform. Missing facts become [CHECK: ...].

[C09] Brands, authenticity and trademark wording
Use it when: Your item is branded, looks like a brand, or you are tempted to write "genuine", "authentic", "style", "inspired by" or "dupe".
----------------------------------------
Check the brand and authenticity wording in my [PLATFORM] listing.

1. List every brand, designer, character, team or trademark name in it.
2. For each, say whether the brief shows the item is made or licensed by that brand. If not: Must fix.
3. Flag "style", "inspired by", "dupe", "replica", "1:1" or "same as [BRAND]". Counterfeits are illegal and banned on every major platform, and using another brand's name for searches is against most platforms' rules. Suggest describing the item by its own features.
4. "Genuine" or "authentic": if the brief gives proof (receipt, bought from the brand), state the proof plainly. If not, remove the word and rely on clear photos of labels.
5. Handmade items with a character, crest or logo: I may need the rights holder's permission [CHECK: the platform's intellectual property rules].

UK English. Never help a replica appear genuine. If the brief suggests it may be fake, tell me plainly not to list it as that brand. Not legal advice.

[C11] UK consumer law wording check
Use it when: Your listing or shop has returns, refunds or guarantee wording, or you are not sure whether you are a private seller or a business.
----------------------------------------
Check my returns, refunds and guarantee wording against UK consumer law basics. A practical check, not legal advice.

I sell as a: [PRIVATE SELLER CLEARING MY OWN THINGS / I BUY TO RESELL / I MAKE ITEMS TO SELL / NOT SURE]
Platform: [PLATFORM]
My wording:
[PASTE WORDING]

1. Status: buying to resell or making to sell means I am likely a trader, even on a personal account. If NOT SURE, list the factors looked at (buying to resell, how often, profit motive) and tell me to check gov.uk. Do not decide for me.
2. Trader: flag wording that limits buyers' rights ("no refunds", "sold as seen", "buyer pays return costs even if faulty"). Buyers from traders generally have goods of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and as described; a short-term right to reject faulty goods, generally within 30 days; and for most online orders a 14-day right to cancel, with exceptions such as personalised items.
3. Private seller: the item must still be as described, "no returns" covers change of mind only, and platform protection can still apply.
4. Flag vague guarantees ("guaranteed quality").
5. Suggest fair, clear replacement wording for my status.

UK English. Never suggest wording that denies legal rights. Tell me to check gov.uk, Citizens Advice and the platform's help pages.

[W05] Batch accuracy check before you post
Use it when: You have a batch of listings ready and want a second pair of eyes to spot invented details, missing flaws and rule problems.
----------------------------------------
Act as a careful UK listings checker. For each item, compare the listing with its brief and report:
1. Any detail NOT in the brief (possible invention).
2. Any flaw in the brief that is missing or softened.
3. Title length problems (eBay UK over 80 characters; other platforms [CHECK: current limit]).
4. Hype, keyword stuffing, misleading or health claims, fake urgency or other platform names.
5. American spellings or US sizes.

One short row per item: Item number | Problems found | Suggested fix. If fine, write "No problems found". Do not rewrite whole listings. UK English.

[W06] Weekly listing routine planner
Use it when: You want a realistic weekly plan that fits your evenings and weekends, so listing does not pile up.
----------------------------------------
Help me plan a weekly listing routine. UK English. Realistic, not motivational.

- Time I have: [E.G. MONDAY AND WEDNESDAY EVENINGS 1 HOUR, SATURDAY MORNING 2 HOURS]
- Items I want to list each week: [NUMBER]
- Platforms: [LIST]
- What slows me down most: [E.G. PHOTOS, MEASURING, WRITING, POSTING]
- Drop-off options near me: [E.G. LOCKER, 24 HOURS]

Give me:
1. A day-by-day table: Day, Time, Task, Roughly how many items, Prompts to use (by ID, e.g. W2, W5, R prompts, M prompts).
2. Batch similar tasks: all photos in one go, all measuring in one go, all writing in one AI session.
3. A 10-minute daily check for messages and dispatch.
4. A weekly 20-minute review: what sold, what has had no interest, what to refresh or reprice.

Simple enough to follow on a phone. Do not promise any sales results.

- Vinted: short plain title, description with measurements and condition, field values.
- Depop: description starting with the key details, up to 5 relevant hashtags.
- Etsy (handmade, vintage of 20 years or more, or craft supplies only): readable title under 140 characters, description, 13 tags of 20 characters or fewer.

Rules:
- Same facts on every platform, from the brief only. Change format and tone, not facts.
- Missing facts become [CHECK: ...].
- No other platform named inside a listing. No hype, stuffing or misleading claims.
- Tell me if the item does not suit a platform instead of forcing it.
